title: Gator Crawl: an alligator museum game
notes:
A solo notebook game for kids. A puppet at the Alligator Museum could sell it.

Each page is a hand-drawn map of a New Orleans spot (French Quarter, City Park, Garden District, a museum after hours). You guide a young alligator on a scavenger hunt.

- **Turn:** roll two dice, one for distance and one for direction, then draw the path in pencil without crossing it.
- **Hunt:** each page lists 5 things to find (praline, brass trumpet, beignet, lost Mardi Gras bead). Circle one when your path reaches it.
- **Trouble:** reaching a tour group, streetcar or museum guard costs a "chomp". Three chomps end the page.
- **Score:** items found plus unused steps. Beating your best unlocks the next landmark, with a final page at a jazz club.
- **Two players:** race on the same map in two colours.

title: Have the website be the second player when a second player is not available.
notes: Word Fleet would just be a general opponent that talks back and forth Oregon Trail style. Other games good reveal solutions or hints based on specific puzzle.

title: Reveal-one-at-a-time device
notes:
A printable device that shows only one item at a time.

- **Dial version:** a paper sleeve with a window. Dial a letter and a number, and the window reveals what belongs at that coordinate.
- **Punch version:** punch a hole at a coordinate on the top sheet, and the answer shows through from the paper underneath.
